T: Rob from the rich. Feed the hungry.
D: A fox in Sherwood Forest robs the greedy Prince John to give back to the poor.
P: Serve the mains when the outlaws celebrate in Sherwood Forest.
S: the outlaws' picnic in the forest

Pork pies, crusty bread, aged cheddar, pickled onions and apples laid out on a cloth. Spread a cloth on the floor or table. Lay out 4 small pork pies, torn crusty bread, wedges of aged cheddar, a jar of pickled onions and sliced green apples. Let everyone help themselves like outlaws picnicking in the forest.
the archery tournament where Robin wins in disguise
Chicken and capsicum threaded onto long skewers, marinated in honey and mustard, grilled until charred.
Friar Tuck's dripping toast with mushrooms
Friar Tuck feeding his poor parish

Thick sourdough fried golden in beef dripping, piled with garlicky thyme mushrooms and a crack of pepper, a humble feed for the parish. Melt 3 tbsp beef dripping in a large frying pan and fry 4 thick slices of sourdough for 2 minutes a side until golden and crisp, then keep warm. Add 20g butter to the pan and fry 400g sliced mixed mushrooms over high heat for 5 minutes, then add 2 crushed garlic cloves and thyme leaves and cook 1 minute more. Season, pile onto the toast and add chopped parsley.
M: the phony king of England counting his taxes

Mustard and thyme crusted beef roasted pink, with puffy Yorkshire puddings, crunchy roast potatoes and a rich onion gravy fit for a greedy prince. Rub a 1.5kg beef topside with 1 tbsp English mustard, thyme and salt and roast at 200C for 50 minutes for medium, with 1kg parboiled potato chunks in oil around it. Rest 20 minutes. Whisk 150g plain flour, 3 eggs and 300ml milk. Heat 1 tsp oil in each hole of a 12-hole muffin tin at 230C, pour in the batter and bake 20 minutes. Fry 1 sliced onion, add 1 tbsp flour and 400ml beef stock and simmer.
Lamb neck, barley, carrots and leeks simmered 2 hours in stock with rosemary, served with crusty bread.
W: the gold taken back from Prince John
Small honey cakes baked at 175C for 15 minutes, glazed with honey and topped with a chocolate coin.
K: Merry Men hot spiced apple punch

Cloudy apple juice mulled with cinnamon, cloves, orange and a little honey, ladled hot into mugs round the Sherwood campfire. Pour 1.5L cloudy apple juice into a saucepan with 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves, 2 strips of orange peel, the juice of 1 orange and 2 tbsp honey. Warm over low heat for 15 minutes without boiling so the spices infuse. Strain and ladle into 4 mugs, each with an orange slice and a cinnamon stick. For a chilled version, cool and top with sparkling apple juice.

s.how: Spread a cloth on the floor or table. Lay out 4 small pork pies, torn crusty bread, wedges of aged cheddar, a jar of pickled onions and sliced green apples. Let everyone help themselves like outlaws picnicking in the forest.

s.note: the archery tournament where Robin wins in disguise
s.how: Cut 600g chicken thighs and 2 red capsicums into chunks and thread onto long skewers. Marinate in honey, wholegrain mustard and crushed garlic for an hour. Grill until charred and cooked through. Aim straight for the centre of the platter.

m.how: Brown 1kg lamb neck pieces, then add 150g pearl barley, 3 sliced carrots, 2 sliced leeks, rosemary and 1.5L water. Simmer for 2 hours until the lamb falls from the bone. Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread around the campfire.

w.note: the gold taken back from Prince John
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 125g honey, then beat in 2 eggs. Fold in 200g self-raising flour. Spoon into patty pans and bake at 175C for 15 minutes. Brush with warm honey and press a gold chocolate coin on top of each. Take from the rich, give to the table.
